prose_updates.tldr: One randomized panel of deterministic machine-learning policies must support sharp causal validation of a prespecified update library. The exact finite-\(\Gamma\) nearest-matching-score width is attained by common homogeneous endpoint schedules both in the aggregate mean class and in its source-faithful individual-level Lipschitz realization. Over the actual no-Lipschitz Chen--Oberst class the exact prospective cost is binary, and the two design objectives meet at the explicit finite-library threshold \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}\): panelwise widths, optimal values, all optimal panels, the mixed-integer program, and independently checked certificates then coincide. The optimal width is nondecreasing and finitely piecewise linear in \(\Gamma\), and is constant beyond the threshold. This objective-level saturation does not equate the underlying response classes. Simultaneous assignment-only coverage remains the supporting inference result.

project_justification.gap: ChenOberst2025 supplies tight monotonicity-only reusable-validation bounds under unit-level performance monotonicity and neutral-action equality, but not the finite-\(\Gamma\) prospective nearest-score identity or the finite-score saturation elbow. AnthonyGoyalGuptaNagarajan2010 supplies the robust scenario nearest-facility skeleton, while generic exact-proof-log work motivates independently checkable optimization records but does not provide the causal cost derivation, the saturation equivalence, or the specialized deterministic rational workflow proved here.
project_justification.niche: The field niche is an exact causal design path over fixed finite policy libraries. A faithful bridge validates the finite-\(\Gamma\) common-schedule width on an individual-level Chen--Oberst Lipschitz subclass; a separate theorem gives the genuine no-Lipschitz binary geometry; and the finite-score saturation theorem proves where the two panel objectives, full minimizer sets, and certificates become identical without asserting equality of response classes.
project_justification.fill: The project proves common sharp endpoint schedules, attained prospective causal-width identities in the finite-Lipschitz and no-Lipschitz regimes, a nondecreasing finite piecewise-linear optimal-width path with an explicit constant tail, a rational budget-optimal mixed-integer panel formulation, simultaneous randomization-only outer coverage, and an exact deterministic certificate workflow. At and above the computable saturation threshold, literal binary-cost substitution preserves the mixed-integer problem and every exact checker comparison.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen and Oberst (2025, Introduction, Section 4, Remark 3.1, and Appendix D.1) study reusable validation under bounded unit-level performance monotonicity and unit-level neutral-action equality, without a Lipschitz restriction, and prove tight bounds. The present conditional-mean monotonicity and neutral invariance are relaxations in aggregation, whereas finite \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz smoothness is a refinement; the two unrestricted classes are incomparable. A homogenization bridge proves that the individual-level \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz subclass and aggregate class generate the same mean surfaces. A separate no-Lipschitz theorem recovers the exact Chen--Oberst binary exact-score or neutral matching geometry, and the new finite-score theorem shows that the finite-\(\Gamma\) panel objective reaches that binary objective at a computable threshold over the fixed libraries. This is equality of design objectives and optimal panels, not equality of the underlying classes. Anthony, Goyal, Gupta, and Nagarajan (2010, Section 2 and Theorem 2.2) supply the robust min--max \(k\)-median skeleton; the metric lift is informed by that result and does not claim its approximation theory. Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy (2017) and Szeider (2026) motivate independently checkable rational proof logs; the present result specializes that goal to the causal action-score tensor through a finite branch generator, exact bounded audit, computable compression condition, and now a binary-cost saturation transfer. The NP-hardness boundary rules out an implied unrestricted polynomial-time guarantee unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\). Causal finite-sample randomization inference and adaptive policy evaluation remain distinct from the fixed-panel optimization question.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The common endpoint schedules establish simultaneous marginal lower and upper endpoints, not rectangularity of the full joint value set. The finite-score threshold compares panel loss functionals over fixed finite candidate and future libraries; it does not make the aggregate finite-Lipschitz class equal to the unrestricted individual-level Chen--Oberst class. If future libraries become denser, the smallest positive relevant score gap may shrink and the saturation threshold may increase. The exact certificate generator may enumerate every feasible panel and its branch tree may be exponential. The polynomial certificate conclusion remains conditional on a feasible panel attaining every full-library coordinatewise residual minimum. The outer confidence intervals are conservative rather than shortest, and scores, libraries, \(\Gamma\), and the budget are fixed before assignment.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The field contributions are the common causal endpoint schedules, exact prospective widths derived from observationally indistinguishable fixed arrays, the faithful bridge to the individual-level Chen--Oberst class, the finite-score saturation elbow, and simultaneous assignment-only coverage. The finite-\(\Gamma\) identity is exact on the individual-level Lipschitz subclass and on the aggregate mean class because their induced mean surfaces coincide. The published no-Lipschitz class instead has the proved binary prospective cost. At and above \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}\), those two finite-library design objectives have the same panelwise values, optimum, full minimizer set, mixed-integer coefficients, and certificate checks; no equality of the response classes is claimed. The certificate workflow is exact and terminating but not polynomial-time on unrestricted instances. The project does not claim a rectangular joint value set, optimal allocation, estimation of future scores, or a saturation threshold uniform over expanding or infinite policy libraries.
